title: Identification of the actual scalar pullback realization maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes $W$ below are noetherian and finite dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, with the meaning and the common full integral constructible categories of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $R_{E,W}=\lim_{n\geq1}(A_{E,n})_W$ on the small pro-etale site, and use framework and PBC completed pullbacks $F^s_{h,E},F^p_{h,E}$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Write $I_{W,E}$ for restriction along the quotient-normalized coefficient identity, giving the integral identity equivalence. All equalities below use these fixed identity transports; we suppress $I$ when source and target already have the same module presentation. For a scheme isomorphism $h:U\simeq T$, let $G_{h,E}$ be ordinary derived module pullback on the completed rings. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ over $R_{E,T}$ set
$$Q_{h,E}(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T),\qquad H(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Q)[-1],$$
with the actual quotient transitions and $s_Q((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].
For each such tower, use the normalized derived comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison],
$$\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q,$$
where $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms and $\iota_I:\lim I_\bullet\to H(I_\bullet)$ has coordinates $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Write $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}:IF^s_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,E}I$ for this comparison with the defining realization identifications, and $b^{\rm int}_{h,E}$ for its restriction to the full integral constructible categories.
Fix an inclusion $E\subset L$ (allowing equality). Put $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ and let $S_W$ be framework completed scalar extension, with the specified quotient/zero-coordinate comparison $\chi_W:C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_W$ on complete objects [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. On a flat-term K-flat $P\to K$ set $P'=P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}R_{L,T}$. Let $d_\bullet:C_UQ_{h,E}(P)\to Q_{h,L}(P')$ be the specified entire strict tower map of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha], with its coefficient generator formula and actual quotient transitions, and let $\delta^s:C_UF^s_{h,E}\to F^s_{h,L}C_T$ be its map on both Roos cone coordinates. Let
$$\delta^p:C_UF^p_{h,E}\longrightarrow F^p_{h,L}C_T$$
be $R\lim(d_\bullet)$ preceded by the canonical finite-free tensor/limit comparison [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-strict-tower-transport], with the defining realization identifications. Then $\delta^p$ is exactly the actual integral PBC scalar/pullback comparison $\alpha^p:C_UF^p_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,L}C_T$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], with its ordinary balanced tensor mate and its completion units retained. Explicitly, for $F=E,L$ let $\kappa^p_{h,F}:G_{h,F}\to F^p_{h,F}$ be the actual PBC completion unit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and let $\theta_h:C_UG_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,L}C_T$ be the ordinary scalar-adjunction mate, which after the coefficient structure isomorphisms $h^{-1}R_{F,T}\cong R_{F,U}$ is represented on flat-term K-flat complexes by the inverse of the balanced-tensor comparison of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Then $\alpha^p$ is the map determined by
$$\alpha^p_K\circ C_U(\kappa^p_{h,E,K})=\kappa^p_{h,L,C_TK}\circ\theta_{h,K}$$
for complete $K$; it is determined because $C_U$ carries the completion unit to a completion unit [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-completion-transport] and $F^p_{h,L}C_TK$ is complete.
For the specified framework comparison $\alpha^s:S_UF^s_{h,E}\to F^s_{h,L}S_T$ one has
$$\alpha^s=F^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\circ\delta^s\circ\chi_{U,F^s_{h,E}}^{-1}=\mu_h^{-1}\lambda_h,$$
where $\lambda,\mu$ belong to the fixed simultaneous realization system of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. More precisely, $\lambda_h\chi_U$ and $\mu_hF^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\delta^s$ are equal to the same whole-tower augmented realization induced by the unshifted level-$m$ projection followed by $d_m$, with zero shifted augmentation coordinate. These identities are natural and independent of resolutions; they assert no invertibility of an individual $d_m$ and no flatness of $A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$.

proof.text: Use the common strict-tower models for the fixed identity transports and their resolution-independent comparison $b$. The completed coefficient sheaf $R_{L,W}$ is finite free over $R_{E,W}$. Exact countable products on the small pro-etale site verify the hypothesis of the strict Roos theorem; finite-free tensor/limit transport applies to entire augmented towers. Thus its augmentation formula may be used with $Q_{h,E}(P)$; no quotient term is being assumed K-flat over $R_{E,U}$. The specified scalar-comparison theorem makes $P'=P\otimes R_{L,T}$ a flat-term K-flat representative of $C_TK$.

proof.text: Write $\gamma_{F,m}:G_{h,F}P_F\to Q_{h,F}(P_F)_m$ for the quotient augmentation. The ordinary mate $\theta_h$ is the inverse balanced-tensor comparison, so on a local generator $x=h^{-1}p$ it sends $x\otimes s$ to $h^{-1}p\otimes s$ with the transported action. Substitute $\bar a=b=1$ into the specified formula for $d_m$. Both $d_m C_U(\gamma_{E,m})$ and $\gamma_{L,m}\theta_h$ send $x\otimes s$ to $h^{-1}(p\otimes1)\otimes\pi^L_m(s)$. Balancing and sheafification extend this equality to modules and termwise to complexes. Since the coefficient maps preserve all quotient transitions, this is an equality of strict augmented tower maps, not an inference from separate derived evaluations.

proof.text:
By the definition of completed pullback, the realization of $\gamma_{F,\bullet}$ is the actual unit $\kappa^p_{h,F}$. Apply the augmentation identity for finite-free tensor/limit transport to step 2, and then apply $R\lim(d_\bullet)$. The result is
$$\delta^p_K C_U(\kappa^p_{h,E,K})=\kappa^p_{h,L,C_TK}\theta_{h,K}.$$
The normalized Roos theorem sends each zero-shifted-coordinate augmentation to this same derived-limit augmentation, so this computation retains the stipulated realization identifications.

proof.text: Put $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$. In the DVR $\mathcal O_L$, the image of $t$ is $wv^e$ with $w$ a unit and $e\geq1$: use its unique unit-times-uniformizer factorization and the fact $0<|t|_L=|t|_E<1$. Apply finite-free completion transport. It identifies $C_U(\kappa^p_{h,E})$ with the completion unit of $C_UG_{h,E}$. The reflector Hom bijection therefore makes precomposition with this map injective into the complete object $F^p_{h,L}C_TK$.

proof.text:
For clarity identify the specified PBC map itself. Let $\tau:C_U\Lambda_E\simeq\Lambda_L C_U$ be unit-normalized completion transport. The reflected coefficient square, applied to ordinary pullback and the inverse balancing $\theta_h^{-1}$, gives the PBC scalar comparison in the orientation of the question as
$$\alpha^p=\Lambda_L(\theta_h)\tau_{G_{h,E}}.$$
Indeed the reflected-square formula gives its inverse $\tau^{-1}\Lambda_L(\theta_h^{-1})$; these are exactly the completed scalar/pullback comparisons of the PBC scalar-extension package. Unit naturality and $\tau C_U(\eta_E)=\eta_L$ give $\alpha^p C_U(\kappa^p_E)=\kappa^p_L\theta_h$. Compare with step 3 and cancel by step 4 to obtain $\delta^p=\alpha^p$, with the actual ordinary mate and completion units.

proof.text:
The specified framework scalar theorem already identifies its actual comparison with
$$\alpha^s=F^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\delta^s\chi_U^{-1}.$$
Here $\delta^s$ acts by $\prod d_m$ on BOTH cone coordinates. It remains to compare with the chosen $\lambda,\mu$, rather than replace them by arbitrary isomorphisms. Use the simultaneous realization system furnished by augmentation/counit matching. Under its normalized Roos maps, the projection from $H(Q_E)$ to $Q_{E,m}$ is the unshifted coordinate $a_m$; the complete family is the whole derived-tower counit $\epsilon_{Q_E}$. Scalar change of this counit, followed by the quotient-module actions, is exactly the family used in the definition of $\lambda$.

proof.text: Compare the whole-tower adjuncts of $\lambda_h\chi_U$ and $\mu_hF^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\delta^s$. For the first, the scalar completion map has coordinates $(0,(z\bmod\varpi_L^m)_m)$. Tensoring the whole counit with the quotient action therefore gives the arrow induced by $a_m$ followed by $d_m$. For the second, substitute the same completion-map formula at $T$ into the defining pullback of the whole counit for $\mu$. The reduction/realization counit composed with reduction of this unit cancels by the adjunction triangle identity. The remaining arrow is again $d_\bullet$ composed with the scalar-changed entire counit of $Q_E$. Counit substitution guarantees this cancellation in the derived category of quotient systems, including tower homotopies; it is not just equality of its evaluations. The balanced action on a generator in both routes is $h^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a))\otimes\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)$. In both augmentations the shifted coordinate is zero. The constant-tower/limit Hom bijection now identifies the two realized arrows. Cancel $\mu$ and $\chi_U$ to obtain $\alpha^s=\mu^{-1}\lambda$.

proof.text: All tensor maps, the normalized Roos comparison, the augmented-limit comparison and the whole-system counit substitutions above are natural derived transformations independent of the chosen resolutions by the cited statements. Hence the equations descend to $K$ and restrict through the full common integral constructible subcategories. The ordinary mate requires no flatness of the finite ring map, and the argument never cancels any $d_m$: only the completion universal property and the specified realization isomorphisms are cancelled. Thus it also applies to ramified extensions and to $E=L$.
